results.title: Groups with a normal p-complement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has a normal $p$-complement when it has a normal subgroup $N$ and a Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ that are complements of each other: every element of $G$ can be written uniquely as $nq$ with $n \in N$ and $q \in P$.

results.title: Gorshkov's problem on maximal p-parts of class sizes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$, the $p$-part of a positive integer $m$ is the largest power of $p$ dividing $m$. This is the statement that for every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and every $p$-element $g$ of $G$ (that is, $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$), if for every $x \in G$ the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $x$ is at most the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $g$, then $G$ has a…

results.title: A maximal p-part of a class size does not force a normal p-complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$, the $p$-part of a positive integer $m$ is the largest power of $p$ dividing $m$. There exist a finite group $G$, a prime $p$ and a $p$-element $g$ of $G$ (that is, $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$) such that for every $x \in G$ the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $x$ is at most the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $g$, but $G$ has no normal $p$-complement.

results.title: Solvability of $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and nonzero elements $a, b \in F$, the equation $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$ is solvable over $F$ if there exist $x, y \in F$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$.

results.title: Hilbert symbol of a field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and nonzero elements $a, b \in F$, the Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_F$ is the integer $1$ if there exist $x, y \in F$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$, and $-1$ otherwise.

results.title: The Hilbert symbol of a field is $\pm 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and all nonzero $a, b \in F$, the Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_F$ of $a$ and $b$ over $F$ equals $1$ or $-1$.

results.title: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ is the integer $1$ if there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$, and $-1$ otherwise.

results.title: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $1$ if and only if there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$.

results.title: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $-1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $-1$ if and only if there are no $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$.

results.title: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $\pm 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and all nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $1$ or $-1$.

results.title: Unit diagonal forms in at least three variables over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ are isotropic for odd $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Unit diagonal forms in at least three variables over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ are isotropic for odd $p$. Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $n > 2$, and let $a_1, \dots, a_n$ be units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Then there is a nonzero vector $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Q}_p^n$ with $a_1 x_1^2 + \dots + a_n x_n^2 = 0$.

results.title: Real Hilbert symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For nonzero real numbers $a$ and $b$, the real Hilbert symbol of $a$ and $b$ is the integer $1$ if there are real numbers $x, y$ with $a x^2 + b y^2 = 1$, and the integer $-1$ otherwise.

results.title: Real Hilbert symbol equal to $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonzero real numbers $a$ and $b$, the real Hilbert symbol of $a$ and $b$ equals $1$ if and only if there are real numbers $x, y$ with $a x^2 + b y^2 = 1$.

results.title: Real Hilbert symbol equal to $-1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonzero real numbers $a$ and $b$, the real Hilbert symbol of $a$ and $b$ equals $-1$ if and only if there are no real numbers $x, y$ with $a x^2 + b y^2 = 1$.

results.title: Sign rule for the real Hilbert symbol
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonzero real numbers $a$ and $b$, the real Hilbert symbol of $a$ and $b$ equals $-1$ if and only if $a < 0$ and $b < 0$.

results.title: The real Hilbert symbol is $\pm 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonzero real numbers $a$ and $b$, the real Hilbert symbol of $a$ and $b$ equals $1$ or $-1$.

results.title: Inclusion of $p$-adic integer units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$, this is the map from the units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ to the units of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ induced by the inclusion $\mathbb{Z}_p \subseteq \mathbb{Q}_p$.

results.title: Value of the inclusion of $p$-adic integer units
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p$, the image of $u$ under the inclusion of the units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ into the units of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, equals $u$ viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

results.title: For odd $p$, a binary unit form over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ represents a unit square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $u, v$ be units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Then there are $x_0, y_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ and a unit $z_0$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with $z_0^2 = u x_0^2 + v y_0^2$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients along an orthonormal family tend to `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(v_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be an orthonormal family in $H$ and let $x \in H$. Then the inner products $\langle v_i, x \rangle$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|\langle v_i, x \rangle| < \varepsilon$ for all but finitely many $i$.

results.title: An orthonormal family tends weakly to `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(v_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be an orthonormal family in $H$ and let $f : H \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional. Then $f(v_i)$ tends to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|f(v_i)| < \varepsilon$ for all but finitely many $i$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients along an orthonormal sequence tend to `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(v_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be an orthonormal sequence in $H$ and let $x \in H$. Then $\langle v_n, x \rangle \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: An orthonormal sequence tends weakly to `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(v_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be an orthonormal sequence in $H$. Then for every continuous linear functional $f : H \to \mathbb{K}$, we have $f(v_n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: An orthonormal sequence does not converge strongly to `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(v_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be an orthonormal sequence in $H$. Then $v_n$ does not tend to $0$ in norm as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: The Gaussian is a Schwartz function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. Then there is a real-valued Schwartz function $g$ on $E$ such that $g(x) = e^{-\|x\|^2}$ for every $x \in E$.

results.title: Values of STLC
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value exactly when it is a lambda abstraction.

results.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: One-step reduction on terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is the least relation closed under three left-to-right call-by-value rules: if $f$ reduces to $f'$, then the application $f\,a$ reduces to $f'\,a$; if $f$ is a value and $a$ reduces to $a'$, then $f\,a$ reduces to $f\,a'$; and if $a$ is a value, then the application of the abstraction of $b$ to $a$ reduces to $b[a]$, the result of substituting $a$ for…

results.title: Values are irreducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value, then there is no term $t'$ to which $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step.

results.title: Canonical forms for closed function values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a term $f$ of function type $A \Rightarrow B$ in the empty context is a value, then $f$ is a lambda abstraction: there is a term $b$ of type $B$ in the one-variable context $[A]$ such that $f$ is the abstraction of $b$.

results.title: Progress for closed STLC terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context is either a value or reduces in one call-by-value step to some term $t'$.

results.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC is deterministic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For terms $t$, $t_1$, $t_2$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, if $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step both to $t_1$ and to $t_2$, then $t_1 = t_2$.

results.title: Normal forms for call-by-value reduction in STLC
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is in normal form when there is no term $t'$ such that $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-value step.

results.title: Closed normal forms are exactly the values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context is in normal form, that is, has no call-by-value reduction step, if and only if it is a value.

results.title: Multi-step call-by-value reduction in STLC
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, multi-step reduction is the reflexive transitive closure of one-step call-by-value reduction.

results.title: Big-step call-by-value evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Fix a typing context $\Gamma$. For terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type in context $\Gamma$, the big-step evaluation relation $t \Downarrow v$ is the least relation such that every lambda abstraction $\lambda.\,b$ evaluates to itself, and an application $f\,a$ evaluates to $v$ whenever $f \Downarrow \lambda.\,b$, $a \Downarrow u$ and $b[u] \Downarrow v$, where $b[u]$ is the body $b$ with its newest free variable…

results.title: Big-step evaluation produces values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the call-by-value simply typed lambda calculus, if a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ evaluates by big-step evaluation to a term $v$, written $t \Downarrow v$, then $v$ is a value, that is, a lambda abstraction.

results.title: Values evaluate to themselves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every value $v$, that is, every lambda abstraction, of any type in any typing context evaluates to itself in the big-step semantics: $v \Downarrow v$.

results.title: Big-step evaluation implies small-step evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same typing context. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$, then $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps.

results.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward reduction steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one left-to-right call-by-value step and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.

results.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward multi-step reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.

results.title: Small-step evaluation to a value implies big-step evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same typing context. If $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, then $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.

results.title: Big-step evaluation is small-step evaluation to a value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type in the same typing context, $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$, if and only if $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, that is, a lambda abstraction.

results.title: Determinism of big-step evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, if a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ evaluates in the big-step call-by-value semantics both to $v$ and to $w$, written $t \Downarrow v$ and $t \Downarrow w$, then $v = w$.

results.title: Closed simply typed terms have a big-step evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type $A$ and every closed term $t$ of type $A$, that is, a term in the empty typing context, there is a term $v$ such that $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-value semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.

results.title: Termination in terms of big-step evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every closed term $t$ of type $A$, that is, a term in the empty typing context, $t$ terminates (it reduces to a value in finitely many left-to-right call-by-value steps) if and only if there is a term $v$ such that $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.
